briefing.opening: Good morning/afternoon. We will now begin the climate briefing for October 14, 2026.

sections.title: 🔴 Crisis Warning for Marine Ecosystems and Domestic Fisheries
sections.content: A chilling warning from a Pukyong National University research team, stating that the squid catch in the East Sea could effectively become '0' by 2040, has been reported by various media outlets [3, 6, 7, 9]. This starkly illustrates the fatal impact of climate change on domestic marine ecosystems and key fish species. In response to this situation, the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries has begun to provisionally offer a 3-month outlook report on marine climate change, with plans to release it every three months going forward [2, 5]. This provision of information is expected to play a crucial role in helping fishing communities adapt to the changing marine environment and prepare for the future.

sections.title: ⚠️ Complex Disasters and Agricultural Impacts of Climate Change
sections.content: Domestically, complex disasters involving a combination of heatwaves and heavy rainfall have continued into autumn, leading to criticism that the existing three-month summer response system is insufficient [11]. This climate change is exacerbating difficulties for the livestock industry in Gyeongsangnam-do, coupled with rising feed costs [1], and in the agricultural sector, efforts to strengthen pest and disease control and introduce AI farming are being called for to address climate change [8, 10]. Meanwhile, in Nepal, a major flood has continued for 50 days, with the unfortunate news that the whereabouts of 9 missing South Koreans remain unconfirmed [103], and the extensive impacts of climate change are being observed in various aspects of daily life, such as the 144 regular season professional baseball games being played amidst record-breaking heatwaves [105]. Furthermore, global research has been published indicating that men's diets have a more detrimental impact on the climate than women's diets [17], suggesting the need for lifestyle habit improvements.

sections.title: 🌱 Expansion of Domestic Carbon Neutrality Policies and Practices
sections.content: Domestically, various policies and citizen-led efforts to achieve carbon neutrality are expanding. The National Institute of Meteorological Sciences' Climate Change Prediction Research Team will continue its operations until 2029, strengthening support for carbon neutrality policies [4], and international verification under the Paris Agreement has gained momentum, with the number of transparency verification cases exceeding 100 [21]. Gwangmyeong City is operating 'Climate Week' to encourage citizen-led carbon neutrality practices [23, 24, 25, 32, 45, 69], and various local governments, including Gyeongsan City and Yeoncheon County, are also spreading carbon neutrality practices through movements like the Saemaul Environmental Preservation campaign or electronic receipt issuance campaigns [26, 33, 34, 38, 71, 75]. Furthermore, waste-to-energy conversion is being proposed as a solution for carbon neutrality, with active international discussions on the topic [39, 42, 48, 50, 54], and efforts to achieve carbon neutrality through education and citizen participation are continuing, such as Seongbuk-gu's Carbon Neutrality Learning Center being designated as an excellent environmental education program [36].

sections.title: 🇰🇷 Opportunities and Challenges of Renewable Energy Transition
sections.content: Concerns have been raised that global big tech companies are building new fossil fuel power generators for AI data center construction, which could effectively be interpreted as abandoning or postponing carbon neutrality goals [31]. While the power grid is identified as a bottleneck for energy transition in the AI era [83], the Trump administration's push to re-evaluate offshore wind project permits is adding uncertainty to renewable energy projects in the United States [80]. Conversely, domestically, the 'priority grid connection' system for community-participatory renewable energy projects under 1MW has been completed [79], and Siheung City is conducting lectures on renewable energy transition to strengthen its 'Siheung-type RE100' policy capabilities [81, 84, 95, 98, 100], seeking to expand solar power in industrial complexes and public facilities. Solar power supply is also expanding in the Saemangeum Industrial Complex, accelerating the RE100 transition [82, 89, 92, 94, 96], and it has been pointed out that a national-level master plan for the development potential of rural and fishing village renewable energy is urgently needed [90, 99].

sections.title: 🌍 Global Impacts and Responses to Climate Change
sections.content: Climate change is threatening brain health in European regions [107, 109, 115] and directly impacting natural phenomena and human health, such as delaying the peak season for autumn foliage and affecting its colors [112]. Furthermore, housing insurance is being affected by the climate crisis [113], and there have been whistleblowing reports alleging that the insurance industry is manipulating figures in the face of the climate crisis [135]. Rare Karkonosze mountain tundra is threatened by climate change [126], and the Sundarbans region is in need of protection due to climate change and thermal power generation [111], indicating an acceleration of ecosystem destruction in various parts of the world. On a positive note, a new team has been formed to save Antarctic ports from climate change [106, 127, 134], and it has been argued that the World Bank and IMF should lead the financial system in responding to the climate crisis [121]. Meanwhile, alongside an analysis that high-emission countries are not making sufficient efforts to protect health from climate change [130], monitoring and demands for the authenticity of climate action are increasing across the international community, with large-scale 'greenwashing' class-action lawsuits being filed against some companies' 'carbon-neutral' energy pledges [131, 132, 133].

briefing.closing: As you have seen in today's briefing, climate change is having severe impacts across various sectors, both domestically and internationally, and immediate, multifaceted response efforts are urgently needed. This concludes today's climate briefing.
